items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: There was a Frenchman named Georges who was taking care of the departure of the band as none of us could speak French, so he told us when another train would be leaving for Nice and we didn't miss that one.

ctx.x: When the show closed at the Rex, we had a few days to stay before we returned to New York. There had been some talk about taking the show to England but it didn't work out. We received a last minute notice that we were to leave the morning of October 4th. There was a rush to pack and do some last minute shopping for souvenirs.

And because of the last minute notice to leave, Leroy Hardy and I arrived at the railroad station two minutes after the train had left. There was a Frenchman named Georges who was taking care of the departure of the band as none of us could speak French, so he told us when another train would be leaving for Nice and we didn't miss that one.

The conductor came for our tickets later and when he saw them, he started telling us something in French which we did not understand. The train made a few stops and at one station I got off and was standing on the platform when a Frenchman came up and asked me if I was Kid Chocolate. He had probably seen a picture of the Kid in the papers and knew that he was in France. I told him I was not the Kid.
